linearAlgebra: Linear Algebra Helpers

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Source: vignettes/linearAlgebra.Rmd
linearAlgebra.Rmd

Description

Linear algebra helpers in R (R Core Team, 2026): vectorization and half-vectorization, symmetric matrices from their half-vectorization, the duplication matrix and its Moore-Penrose inverse, deviation scores, and tests for symmetric and positive definite matrices. Each exported function has an internal version without input checks that other projects can copy.

Installation

You can install the development version of linearAlgebra from GitHub with:

if (!require("pak")) install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("ijapesigan/linearAlgebra")

Example 

library(package = "linearAlgebra")

A covariance matrix of three variables.

sigma <- stats::cov(x = datasets::mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])
sigma
#>             mpg        wt         hp
#> mpg   36.324103 -5.116685 -320.73206
#> wt    -5.116685  0.957379   44.19266
#> hp  -320.732056 44.192661 4700.86694

Vec() stacks the columns. Vech() stacks the lower triangle with the diagonal, and Vechs() the lower triangle without it.

Vec(x = sigma)
#> [1]   36.324103   -5.116685 -320.732056   -5.116685    0.957379   44.192661
#> [7] -320.732056   44.192661 4700.866935
Vech(x = sigma)
#>     mpg,mpg      wt,mpg      hp,mpg       wt,wt       hp,wt       hp,hp 
#>   36.324103   -5.116685 -320.732056    0.957379   44.192661 4700.866935
Vechs(x = sigma)
#>      wt,mpg      hp,mpg       hp,wt 
#>   -5.116685 -320.732056   44.192661

SymofVech() and SymofVechs() rebuild the symmetric matrix.

SymofVech(x = Vech(x = sigma))
#>             [,1]      [,2]       [,3]
#> [1,]   36.324103 -5.116685 -320.73206
#> [2,]   -5.116685  0.957379   44.19266
#> [3,] -320.732056 44.192661 4700.86694
SymofVechs(x = Vechs(x = sigma), diags = diag(x = sigma))
#>             [,1]      [,2]       [,3]
#> [1,]   36.324103 -5.116685 -320.73206
#> [2,]   -5.116685  0.957379   44.19266
#> [3,] -320.732056 44.192661 4700.86694

The duplication matrix maps the half-vectorization to the vectorization, and its Moore-Penrose inverse maps back.

d_mat <- DMat(k = 3)
all.equal(
  target = as.vector(x = d_mat %*% Vech(x = sigma)),
  current = Vec(x = sigma)
)
#> [1] TRUE
all.equal(
  target = as.vector(x = PInvDmat(k = 3) %*% Vec(x = sigma)),
  current = unname(obj = Vech(x = sigma))
)
#> [1] TRUE

Tests for symmetric and positive definite matrices.

TestSymmetric(x = sigma)
#> [1] TRUE
TestPositiveDefinite(x = sigma)
#> [1] TRUE

Deviation scores.

deviation <- Deviation(
  x = as.matrix(x = datasets::mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt")])
)
utils::head(x = deviation)
#>                         mpg       wt
#> Mazda RX4          0.909375 -0.59725
#> Mazda RX4 Wag      0.909375 -0.34225
#> Datsun 710         2.709375 -0.89725
#> Hornet 4 Drive     1.309375 -0.00225
#> Hornet Sportabout -1.390625  0.22275
#> Valiant           -1.990625  0.24275
